thread:
alex: Hey — found a reproducible edge where token refresh during an SSE stream causes out-of-order fragments + duplicate final token. Repro in the sampleapp with short TTL (30s) tokens.

maria: ugh. any logs or a tiny repro snippet?

alex: paste:

alex: ```bash
# hit our streaming endpoint repeatedly with short-lived token
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.dev/v1/streams?model=small-repro"
```

alex: observed behavior: sequence ids jump backwards after auth refresh, i.e. seq=113,114,115 then reconnect produces seq=110,111,115-final. client treats 115-final as duplicate and refuses to reassemble -> truncated JSON.

jordan: I've seen this shape before during a canary where refresh produced a new connection with a stale Last-Event-ID header. Two problems: (1) server may emit cached fragments without bumping a monotonic chunk counter, (2) client merge logic assumes monotonic seq.

ci-bot: created issue #3421: "sse: auth-refresh race -> fragment ordering/dup final" (link: https://git.redwood/s/3421)

sam: quick workaround: bump the client to attach a connection-id and accept out-of-order seqs up to window=8 while deduping by chunk-id; or refresh tokens earlier (30s -> 5m). Long-term: SDK should buffer inflight fragments during token refresh and resume with Last-Event-ID mapping.

tess: can you drop the minimal sampleapp steps (docker env) so I can add to CI repro matrix?

alex: steps:
1) git checkout reproducer branch alex/stream-sse-refresh
2) docker-compose up sampleapp (it uses dev auth proxy that issues 30s tokens)
3) run `node ./scripts/stream-repro.js` (attached to thread) which opens SSE, sleeps 25s, forces refresh, then waits for 10s.

alex: log excerpt: 

[2026-03-20T18:12:34Z] OUT seq=113 payload=...
[2026-03-20T18:12:34Z] OUT seq=114 payload=...
[2026-03-20T18:12:59Z] token refresh start
[2026-03-20T18:13:00Z] reconnect start last-event-id=113
[2026-03-20T18:13:00Z] IN seq=110 payload=...  # older fragment resurfaced
[2026-03-20T18:13:01Z] IN seq=111 payload=...
[2026-03-20T18:13:02Z] IN seq=115-final payload=...

maria: interesting. the `last-event-id=113` vs incoming 110 indicates server is replaying cached partial response not aligned to seq namespace. Could be a proxy cache (nginx, edge) returning stale chunk sets. Can you confirm headers on the reconnect?

alex: headers: `Connection: keep-alive, Last-Event-ID: 113, X-Proxy-Cache: MISS` on reconnect attempt, but subsequent body shows old seqs. I suspect the runtime served a cached KV block for the model prefix.

jordan: two remediation paths: (A) enforce strict monotonic chunk ids server-side (monotonic stream generation + attach global stream-id + incremental counter), (B) client tolerant merge + explicit resume mapping: treat chunks as {stream_id, chunk_idx} rather than trusting last-event-id alone.

sam: I'll sketch an SDK change:

```js
// on auth refresh: pause consumer, finish current parse frame, hold partials in buffer
await auth.refresh();
reopen connection with header: Last-Event-ID=buffered.latest_chunk_id
apply any buffered fragments on resume merge by stream_id
```

sam: also add an opt-in env var REDWOOD_SSE_STRICT=true to failfast on seq regressions in internal e2e tests.

tess: assigned to me to add a deterministic test in devex/sampleapp. Can you attach the `stream-repro.js`?

alex: attached gist link: https://gist.redwood/alex/stream-repro.js (small) — it intentionally forces refresh by calling token endpoint with short TTL.

maria: until SDK fix lands, recommended mitigation for affected customers: increase token TTL or proactively refresh before expected request window. We'll add a note in the streaming SDK docs.

jordan: I'll open a draft PR for server-side monotonic chunk IDs. sam, can you owner the client buffering changes?

sam: yep, will add tests and a feature flag.

alex: thanks folks — adding logs and the minimal repro to issue #3421. If anyone else sees similar in perf envs please drop traces. :thumbsup:
